arm_string_literals: Includes: Pearson chi-square, Fisher’s exact (two-sided, one-sided, mid-p), Odds ratio + CI, Relative risk + CI, McNemar / Liddell test for paired 2×2. Analyze 2×2 contingency tables with exact tests and common effect-size measures.
Includes: Tukey boxplot (median, quartiles, whiskers), Outliers via 1.5×IQR rule. Visualize distribution shape and outliers across one or more groups.
Includes: Bullet Chart. Compare an observed value with a target while simultaneously showing qualitative performance ranges in a compact dashboard-style display.
Includes: Grouped density histograms, stacked density histograms, grouped frequency histograms for unequal sample sizes.
Includes: Cochran’s Q, Percent of 1’s per condition. Test differences in matched binary outcomes across three or more conditions (extension of McNemar).

Includes: Individuals, moving-range, I–MR, X-bar, R, S, X-bar–R, X-bar–S, p, np, c, u, CUSUM, EWMA, and moving-average charts; Phase I and Phase II stages; historical or stage-specific limits; wide and stacked subgroup layouts; exact probability limits for attribute charts; special-cause rule presets and custom rules; explicit exclusions; specification and target lines; detailed chart data, signals, settings, and audit output.
Includes: Convex Hull Plot. Display a point cloud together with the smallest convex boundary containing all observations, either for the complete dataset or separately for each group.
Includes: Correspondence analysis (CA), Row/column contribution plots, Biplot. Explore structure in contingency tables via low-dimensional map representations of rows and columns.

Includes: Cox proportional hazards model, Tie handling: Breslow, Efron, Exact, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, robust variance (optional), residuals + PH score test (optional), baseline + adjusted survival curves. Fit a proportional hazards model to time-to-event data and report hazard ratios with diagnostics.

Includes: Cumulative Distribution Function Plot. Display the cumulative distribution of one or more continuous samples, compare groups across the full distribution, read empirical percentiles, and visually compare observed cumulative behaviour with a fitted theoretical distribution.

Includes: n, mean, median, SD / variance, SEM, CV, skewness / kurtosis, Q1 / Q3, IQR, min / max / range, Shapiro–Wilk (optional). Compute a compact set of summary statistics for one or multiple variables, optionally adding a normality check.

Includes: Linear and quadratic discriminant analysis, group priors, optional preprocessing, posterior probabilities, classification tables, canonical discriminant functions, and leave-one-out / k-fold / holdout validation. Classify observations into known groups and inspect how the groups are separated.

Includes: Dumbbell Plot. Horizontal two-endpoint dumbbell charts, numeric or date/time X axes, optional repeated observations/events. Compare two values for each category while showing both the direction and magnitude of the difference, with optional additional observations displayed along the same horizontal scale.

Includes: Exploratory factor analysis on correlation or covariance matrices; extraction by principal axis, maximum likelihood, generalized least squares, image, alpha, or principal-components style extraction; retention by fixed count / eigenvalue cutoff / cumulative variance; orthogonal or oblique rotation; factor scores; diagnostics; scree and loading plots. Explore latent structure behind correlated numeric variables and inspect communalities, loadings, scores, and residual matrices.

Includes: Friedman test, Post-hoc multiple comparisons (MCP), Descriptive stats (optional), Box plot (optional). Nonparametric repeated-measures alternative to one-way RM ANOVA for ranked data across conditions.

Includes: Families: Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Negative Binomial, Gamma, Covariance structures: Independence, Exchangeable, Autoregressive, Toeplitz, Unstructured, SE types: Robust, Naive, Bias-reduced, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values. Fit marginal models for correlated/clustered data using GEE with selectable working correlation.

Includes: GLM families: Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Negative Binomial, Gamma, Links per family (selectable), categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, optional weights and offset, IRLS with user-set iterations/ε, optional covariance matrix and residuals. Fit generalized linear models to a wide range of outcome types with configurable link functions.

Includes: Agglomerative hierarchical clustering, linkage methods (Ward, complete, average, weighted average, single, centroid, median), distance metrics (squared Euclidean, Euclidean, Manhattan, Chebyshev, Minkowski, cosine, correlation), optional preprocessing, cluster membership by cluster count or cut height, and dendrogram plotting. Explore the full nested cluster structure and visualize it as an Excel dendrogram.

Includes: Automatic bin rules (Sturges, Doane, Scott, Freedman–Diaconis), Overlay multiple groups (optional). Create publication-friendly histograms with sensible bin-width heuristics and optional overlays.

Includes: Fligner–Killeen, Levene (Brown–Forsythe/median), Squared Ranks, Bartlett. Test whether multiple groups have similar variances, which is an important assumption for many parametric comparisons.

Includes: One-sample Hotelling’s T², Two-sample (independent) Hotelling’s T², Paired Hotelling’s T², Simultaneous confidence intervals. Multivariate extension of the t-test for comparing mean vectors (one-sample, two-sample, or paired).

Includes: Sample size for two independent proportions with Superiority, Noninferiority, and Equivalence modes. Estimate sample sizes for comparing two independent proportions (with optional group-size ratio κ).

Includes: Kaplan–Meier survival estimate, Optional confidence bands, Tabular survival output (optional). Plot survival over time and summarize survival probabilities (with censoring) for one or multiple groups.
Includes: Kendall’s τ, p-value / CI where applicable. Measure ordinal association between two variables, with good behavior under ties and small samples.

Includes: Symmetric multi-series kite diagrams, one-range data selection, optional row and column labels, common scaling across series, missing-value gaps, automatic zero-width endpoints, direct series labels, and selectable chart destination.

Includes: K-means clustering for numeric data, initialization by k-means++, Forgy, random partition, or user-specified centers, repeated random starts, optional z-score or 0–1 range standardization, explicit missing-value handling, empty-cluster strategies, and prediction for new observations. Partition observations into a requested number of compact centroid-based clusters.
Includes: H statistic (uncorrected), H statistic (tie-corrected), Dunn’s post-hoc comparisons (optional). Nonparametric one-way ANOVA alternative for comparing more than two independent groups.

Includes: Paired First-Second ladder plots, optional record labels, optional grouping, single-colour by-observation by-group colouring, connected markers, collision-aware horizontal jitter, independent endpoint labels, automatic label-overlap reduction, automatic Y-axis intervals, custom Y-axis limits and number formats, horizontal gridlines, and configurable chart size.
Includes: Logrank, Tarone–Ware, Gehan–Breslow, Peto, Modified Peto (Andersen). Compare survival curves between groups using logrank-type tests (with several common weightings).

Includes: Exact p-values (when available), Normal approximation (ties + continuity correction), Hodges–Lehmann shift estimate (optional). Nonparametric alternative to the two-sample t-test for comparing two independent groups.

Includes: Mantel–Haenszel chi-square, Pooled odds ratio + confidence interval at the selected level. Combine stratified 2×2 tables to estimate a pooled association while controlling for a stratification factor.

Includes: Multinomial logistic regression, Reference category selection (first/last), categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, optional offset/weights, covariance matrix, residuals. Model nominal outcomes with more than two categories.
Includes: Multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) via indicator/Burt matrix, Contribution plots, Biplot. Extend correspondence analysis to multiple categorical variables (survey-style data).

Includes: OLS multiple regression, Optional weights, Type I or Type III term SS (ANOVA table), Optional covariance matrix, residuals, VIF, and partial r. Fit a standard linear regression model, report coefficients, ANOVA-style term tests, and adjusted predictor diagnostics.

Includes: Hotelling T-squared charts for individual observations and rational subgroups, generalized-variance charts for subgroup dispersion, PCA T-squared and PCA Q charts, multivariate EWMA (MEWMA), Crosier multivariate CUSUM (MCUSUM), Phase I and Phase II stages, historical mean/covariance models, exclusions, covariance regularization, rank-deficiency handling, point diagnostics, variable contributions, chart data, signals, settings, and audit output..

Includes: Negative Binomial (NB2) regression, Overdispersion parameter (estimated), categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, optional offset/weights, covariance matrix, residuals. Model overdispersed count outcomes using an NB2 variance function.

Includes: Rank methods: Blom, Rankit, Van der Waerden, Line fits: SPSS, OLS, R-style, Optional descriptive stats. Create a normal probability plot to visually assess normality and identify deviations such as skewness or heavy tails.
Includes: Shapiro–Wilk, D’Agostino–Pearson K², Anderson–Darling. Check whether a sample distribution is consistent with normality—useful before parametric tests.

Includes: Classic one-way ANOVA, Welch ANOVA, Post-hoc: LSD, Bonferroni, Tukey–Kramer, Games–Howell. Compare means across multiple independent groups and run common post-hoc procedures when differences are detected.

Includes: RM ANOVA, Sphericity: Mauchly test (optional), Corrections: Greenhouse–Geisser, Huynh–Feldt (optional), Post-hoc: Tukey (optional), Descriptive stats / box plot (optional). Compare means across repeated conditions for the same subjects, with optional sphericity diagnostics and corrections.

Includes: Ordinal logistic regression, Reference category selection (first/last), categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, optional offset/weights, covariance matrix, residuals. Model ordered categorical outcomes using an ordinal logistic framework.

Includes: Gaussian MMRM, ML / REML, subject-level residual covariance structures, Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger inference, LS-means, contrasts, change from baseline, reference-grid estimated marginal means, diagnostics, and worksheet UDFs. Fit a marginal repeated-measures model for continuous longitudinal outcomes and estimate visit-specific means and treatment differences.

Includes: Gaussian linear mixed models, ML / REML, fixed effects with categorical factors, polynomial terms and interactions, random intercepts, random slopes and random-effect interactions, G-side covariance structures (RI, RI+slope, ID, VC/Diag, CS, CSH, AR1, ARH1, TOEP, TOEPH, Unstructured), optional R-side residual covariance structures, Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger inference, fitted values/residuals, BLUPs, covariance/correlation output, diagnostics and trace output. Fit subject- or cluster-level random-effects models for continuous outcomes, including random-intercept, random-slope and richer mixed-model specifications.

Includes: Propensity score estimation by GLM logistic regression or supplied scores; nearest-neighbor, optimal pair, subclassification, weighting, coarsened exact matching, exact matching restrictions, calipers, common support and trimming; ATT / ATC / ATE / ATO estimands; balance diagnostics, Love-plot data, overlap and weight diagnostics, AIPW doubly robust estimates, bootstrap summaries, and Rosenbaum-style matched-pair sensitivity analysis. Estimate treatment effects for observational studies by balancing treated and control groups using propensity-score-based matching, weighting, and diagnostics.
Includes: Paired t-test (matched pairs). Compare two paired measurements on the same subjects by testing the mean of differences.
Includes: Sample size for paired t-test (iterative t critical values). Estimate required number of pairs for a paired t-test given effect size, SD, α and power.

Includes: Paired radius–angle plots, degrees/radians/percentage angles, clockwise or counterclockwise rotation, four zero-angle positions, optional connecting lines, optional text or numeric grouping, automatic radial scaling, configurable radial and angular tick intervals.

Includes: PCA on correlation or covariance matrix, Component extraction: eigenvalue, fixed k, variance threshold, Outputs: scores, loadings, reduced dataset, Plots: scree, score/loading plots, biplots (2D/3D). Reduce dimensionality of multivariate numeric data and visualize dominant patterns.

Includes: Single proportion (estimate + CI), Two independent proportions (Superiority, Noninferiority, Equivalence) (difference + CI, Fisher exact p-values), Two paired proportions (difference + CI, Liddell/McNemar-type test). Work with binomial outcomes: estimate proportions and compare proportions between groups.
Includes: ROC curve points, AUC (Wilcoxon), SE / CI / p-value, Cutoff table. Assess binary classifier performance and explore sensitivity/specificity tradeoffs across thresholds.

Includes: Pearson chi-square test of independence, Nominal association (Cramer's V, Phi, contingency coefficient), Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test (optional), Ordinal association (tau-b/tau-c, gamma, Somers’ D), Cochran–Armitage trend test (when applicable). Analyze general contingency tables and report association measures and exact/trend tests where applicable.

Includes: Sankey Plot. Weighted Sankey/alluvial diagrams, staged row-by-row pathways, Source/Target link tables, optional frequency or continuous positive weights, automatic or explicit stage placement. Visualize how counts, frequencies, or other non-negative quantities flow between categorical states across two or more stages.
Includes: Scatter plot matrix, Optional correlation coefficients, Optional regression lines. Quickly explore pairwise relationships among many variables.

Includes: Sample size planning for a two-group log-rank test. Estimate the required number of events, plus the corresponding numbers of controls, experimental subjects, and total subjects for a study with a time-to-event endpoint.
Includes: Sample size for a single proportion test. Estimate required sample size for testing a single proportion against a null value.
Includes: Skillings–Mack test (handles missing values). Nonparametric test for block designs like Friedman, but robust to missing observations.
Includes: Spearman’s ρ (rank correlation), p-value / CI where applicable. Measure monotonic association between two variables using ranks (robust to non-normality and outliers).
Includes: Miao–Gel–Gastwirth test, Cabilio–Masaro test, Asymmetry plot (optional). Evaluate whether a distribution is symmetric around its center and visualize asymmetry when needed.
Includes: Median slope (Theil–Sen), CI at the selected level (Sen/large-sample approx.), Robust intercept. Use when you want a robust simple linear trend estimate that resists outliers.

Includes: Two-way nested ANOVA, Balanced design check, Satterthwaite approximation. Analyze hierarchical (nested) designs such as subjects nested within centers, with appropriate variance decomposition.
Includes: Grubbs’ test (single outlier), Rosner / generalized ESD (multiple outliers). Identify statistically unusual values in a single variable, with options suited to one or multiple outliers.

Includes: two-sample t-test for superiority, noninferiority, and equivalence (TOST) for two independent means; choice of Welch unequal variances or equal variances (pooled); optional descriptive statistics and box-and-whiskers plot. Compare two independent groups under (or relaxing) the equal-variance assumption.

Includes: Sample size planning for an unpaired two-sample t-test in Superiority, Noninferiority, and Equivalence modes. Estimate required sample sizes per group for a two-sample t-test given effect size, SD, α and power.

Includes: Event-count and subject-count planning for a Cox proportional hazards model with either a binary covariate or a continuous covariate. /nEstimate the required number of events, and when an overall event proportion is supplied, the corresponding number of subjects..

Includes: Sample size planning for a one-sided hypothesis test on an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). /nEstimate the required number of subjects for a study in which each subject is measured repeatedly or rated multiple times.

Includes: Sample size planning for a Bland-Altman agreement study when the goal is to control the confidence-interval half-width around a limit of agreement (LoA). /nEstimate the required number of paired measurements so that the confidence interval around either LoA is sufficiently precise on the original measurement scale.

Includes: Multi-group categorical violin plots, Gaussian kernel-density estimation, Silverman/Scott/manual bandwidths, bandwidth adjustment, configurable density resolution, equal-width/equal-area/sample-size scaling.

Includes: Exact p-values (when available), Normal approximation (ties + continuity correction), Hodges–Lehmann shift estimate, Sign test (optional). Nonparametric paired comparison test for matched samples or before/after measurements.

Includes: 3D scatter plot (X,Y,Z), Optional group coloring, Optional point labels, Rotation/zoom + plane projections (optional). Visualize three-dimensional relationships with interactive rotation controls.

Includes: ZIP model (Poisson count + logistic inflation part), separate authored effects for the Poisson and Logistic components, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, EM-style fitting (with iterations/ε), optional starting values for both parts. Model count data with excess zeros by combining a Poisson model with a separate zero-inflation process.

Includes: Passing–Bablok nonparametric linear regression for method comparison, slope/intercept estimates, confidence intervals, and robust handling of outliers. Use when comparing two measurement methods without assuming normal errors or homoscedasticity.

Includes: Deming (errors-in-variables) regression with configurable error ratio (λ), weighted/generalized variance models, point estimates and confidence intervals. Use when both X and Y have measurement error and you want a symmetric method-comparison regression.

Includes: Simple paired Bland–Altman analysis, repeated-measures Bland–Altman by subject, bias and limits of agreement (LoA), analytical / jackknife / bootstrap confidence intervals, optional proportional-bias check, optional allowable-bias / decision-limit reporting, raw-difference / percentage / log-ratio scales, several x-axis conventions, and Bland–Altman plots with optional subject means.
Includes: Lin CCC, Pearson r, bias-correction factor Cb, analytical or bootstrap confidence intervals, null-concordance test, and identity-line plot.

Includes: Cohen's / weighted kappa for paired categorical ratings, with unweighted, linear, quadratic, Cicchetti–Allison, and Fleiss–Cohen weighting schemes; analytical and bootstrap confidence intervals; confusion-matrix output; and weight-matrix output.
Includes: ICC(1,1), ICC(1,k), ICC(2,1), ICC(2,k), ICC(3,1), ICC(3,k) with confidence intervals. Quantify reliability/agreement of measurements across raters/replicates using standard ICC families.

        Private Shared Function IndexByKey(items As IEnumerable(Of AnalysisMethodMetadata)) As Dictionary(Of String, AnalysisMethodMetadata)
            Dim result As New Dictionary(Of String, AnalysisMethodMetadata)(StringComparer.Ordinal)
            For Each item As AnalysisMethodMetadata In items
                result.Add(item.Key, item)
            Next
            Return result
        End Function

        Private Shared Function IndexByAnalysisId(items As IEnumerable(Of AnalysisMethodMetadata)) As Dictionary(Of String, AnalysisMethodMetadata)
            Dim result As New Dictionary(Of String, AnalysisMethodMetadata)(StringComparer.Ordinal)
            For Each item As AnalysisMethodMetadata In items
                If item.AnalysisId IsNot Nothing Then result.Add(item.AnalysisId, item)
            Next
            Return result
        End Function

arm_string_literals: Includes: Pearson chi-square, Fisher’s exact (two-sided, one-sided, mid-p), Odds ratio + CI, Relative risk + CI, McNemar / Liddell test for paired 2×2. Analyze 2×2 contingency tables with exact tests and common effect-size measures.
Includes: Tukey boxplot (median, quartiles, whiskers), Outliers via 1.5×IQR rule. Visualize distribution shape and outliers across one or more groups.
Includes: Bullet Chart. Compare an observed value with a target while simultaneously showing qualitative performance ranges in a compact dashboard-style display.
Includes: Grouped density histograms, stacked density histograms, grouped frequency histograms for unequal sample sizes.
Includes: Cochran’s Q, Percent of 1’s per condition. Test differences in matched binary outcomes across three or more conditions (extension of McNemar).

Includes: Individuals, moving-range, I–MR, X-bar, R, S, X-bar–R, X-bar–S, p, np, c, u, CUSUM, EWMA, and moving-average charts; Phase I and Phase II stages; historical or stage-specific limits; wide and stacked subgroup layouts; exact probability limits for attribute charts; special-cause rule presets and custom rules; explicit exclusions; specification and target lines; detailed chart data, signals, settings, and audit output.
Includes: Convex Hull Plot. Display a point cloud together with the smallest convex boundary containing all observations, either for the complete dataset or separately for each group.
Includes: Correspondence analysis (CA), Row/column contribution plots, Biplot. Explore structure in contingency tables via low-dimensional map representations of rows and columns.

Includes: Cox proportional hazards model, Tie handling: Breslow, Efron, Exact, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, robust variance (optional), residuals + PH score test (optional), baseline + adjusted survival curves. Fit a proportional hazards model to time-to-event data and report hazard ratios with diagnostics.

Includes: Cumulative Distribution Function Plot. Display the cumulative distribution of one or more continuous samples, compare groups across the full distribution, read empirical percentiles, and visually compare observed cumulative behaviour with a fitted theoretical distribution.

Includes: n, mean, median, SD / variance, SEM, CV, skewness / kurtosis, Q1 / Q3, IQR, min / max / range, Shapiro–Wilk (optional). Compute a compact set of summary statistics for one or multiple variables, optionally adding a normality check.

Includes: Linear and quadratic discriminant analysis, group priors, optional preprocessing, posterior probabilities, classification tables, canonical discriminant functions, and leave-one-out / k-fold / holdout validation. Classify observations into known groups and inspect how the groups are separated.

Includes: Dumbbell Plot. Horizontal two-endpoint dumbbell charts, numeric or date/time X axes, optional repeated observations/events. Compare two values for each category while showing both the direction and magnitude of the difference, with optional additional observations displayed along the same horizontal scale.

Includes: Exploratory factor analysis on correlation or covariance matrices; extraction by principal axis, maximum likelihood, generalized least squares, image, alpha, or principal-components style extraction; retention by fixed count / eigenvalue cutoff / cumulative variance; orthogonal or oblique rotation; factor scores; diagnostics; scree and loading plots. Explore latent structure behind correlated numeric variables and inspect communalities, loadings, scores, and residual matrices.

Includes: Friedman test, Post-hoc multiple comparisons (MCP), Descriptive stats (optional), Box plot (optional). Nonparametric repeated-measures alternative to one-way RM ANOVA for ranked data across conditions.

Includes: Families: Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Negative Binomial, Gamma, Covariance structures: Independence, Exchangeable, Autoregressive, Toeplitz, Unstructured, SE types: Robust, Naive, Bias-reduced, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values. Fit marginal models for correlated/clustered data using GEE with selectable working correlation.

Includes: GLM families: Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Negative Binomial, Gamma, Links per family (selectable), categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, optional weights and offset, IRLS with user-set iterations/ε, optional covariance matrix and residuals. Fit generalized linear models to a wide range of outcome types with configurable link functions.

Includes: Agglomerative hierarchical clustering, linkage methods (Ward, complete, average, weighted average, single, centroid, median), distance metrics (squared Euclidean, Euclidean, Manhattan, Chebyshev, Minkowski, cosine, correlation), optional preprocessing, cluster membership by cluster count or cut height, and dendrogram plotting. Explore the full nested cluster structure and visualize it as an Excel dendrogram.

Includes: Automatic bin rules (Sturges, Doane, Scott, Freedman–Diaconis), Overlay multiple groups (optional). Create publication-friendly histograms with sensible bin-width heuristics and optional overlays.

Includes: Fligner–Killeen, Levene (Brown–Forsythe/median), Squared Ranks, Bartlett. Test whether multiple groups have similar variances, which is an important assumption for many parametric comparisons.

Includes: One-sample Hotelling’s T², Two-sample (independent) Hotelling’s T², Paired Hotelling’s T², Simultaneous confidence intervals. Multivariate extension of the t-test for comparing mean vectors (one-sample, two-sample, or paired).

Includes: Sample size for two independent proportions with Superiority, Noninferiority, and Equivalence modes. Estimate sample sizes for comparing two independent proportions (with optional group-size ratio κ).

Includes: Kaplan–Meier survival estimate, Optional confidence bands, Tabular survival output (optional). Plot survival over time and summarize survival probabilities (with censoring) for one or multiple groups.
Includes: Kendall’s τ, p-value / CI where applicable. Measure ordinal association between two variables, with good behavior under ties and small samples.

Includes: Symmetric multi-series kite diagrams, one-range data selection, optional row and column labels, common scaling across series, missing-value gaps, automatic zero-width endpoints, direct series labels, and selectable chart destination.

Includes: K-means clustering for numeric data, initialization by k-means++, Forgy, random partition, or user-specified centers, repeated random starts, optional z-score or 0–1 range standardization, explicit missing-value handling, empty-cluster strategies, and prediction for new observations. Partition observations into a requested number of compact centroid-based clusters.
Includes: H statistic (uncorrected), H statistic (tie-corrected), Dunn’s post-hoc comparisons (optional). Nonparametric one-way ANOVA alternative for comparing more than two independent groups.

Includes: Paired First-Second ladder plots, optional record labels, optional grouping, single-colour by-observation by-group colouring, connected markers, collision-aware horizontal jitter, independent endpoint labels, automatic label-overlap reduction, automatic Y-axis intervals, custom Y-axis limits and number formats, horizontal gridlines, and configurable chart size.
Includes: Logrank, Tarone–Ware, Gehan–Breslow, Peto, Modified Peto (Andersen). Compare survival curves between groups using logrank-type tests (with several common weightings).

Includes: Exact p-values (when available), Normal approximation (ties + continuity correction), Hodges–Lehmann shift estimate (optional). Nonparametric alternative to the two-sample t-test for comparing two independent groups.

Includes: Mantel–Haenszel chi-square, Pooled odds ratio + confidence interval at the selected level. Combine stratified 2×2 tables to estimate a pooled association while controlling for a stratification factor.

Includes: Multinomial logistic regression, Reference category selection (first/last), categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, optional offset/weights, covariance matrix, residuals. Model nominal outcomes with more than two categories.
Includes: Multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) via indicator/Burt matrix, Contribution plots, Biplot. Extend correspondence analysis to multiple categorical variables (survey-style data).

Includes: OLS multiple regression, Optional weights, Type I or Type III term SS (ANOVA table), Optional covariance matrix, residuals, VIF, and partial r. Fit a standard linear regression model, report coefficients, ANOVA-style term tests, and adjusted predictor diagnostics.

Includes: Hotelling T-squared charts for individual observations and rational subgroups, generalized-variance charts for subgroup dispersion, PCA T-squared and PCA Q charts, multivariate EWMA (MEWMA), Crosier multivariate CUSUM (MCUSUM), Phase I and Phase II stages, historical mean/covariance models, exclusions, covariance regularization, rank-deficiency handling, point diagnostics, variable contributions, chart data, signals, settings, and audit output..

Includes: Negative Binomial (NB2) regression, Overdispersion parameter (estimated), categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, optional offset/weights, covariance matrix, residuals. Model overdispersed count outcomes using an NB2 variance function.

Includes: Rank methods: Blom, Rankit, Van der Waerden, Line fits: SPSS, OLS, R-style, Optional descriptive stats. Create a normal probability plot to visually assess normality and identify deviations such as skewness or heavy tails.
Includes: Shapiro–Wilk, D’Agostino–Pearson K², Anderson–Darling. Check whether a sample distribution is consistent with normality—useful before parametric tests.

Includes: Classic one-way ANOVA, Welch ANOVA, Post-hoc: LSD, Bonferroni, Tukey–Kramer, Games–Howell. Compare means across multiple independent groups and run common post-hoc procedures when differences are detected.

Includes: RM ANOVA, Sphericity: Mauchly test (optional), Corrections: Greenhouse–Geisser, Huynh–Feldt (optional), Post-hoc: Tukey (optional), Descriptive stats / box plot (optional). Compare means across repeated conditions for the same subjects, with optional sphericity diagnostics and corrections.

Includes: Ordinal logistic regression, Reference category selection (first/last), categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, optional offset/weights, covariance matrix, residuals. Model ordered categorical outcomes using an ordinal logistic framework.

Includes: Gaussian MMRM, ML / REML, subject-level residual covariance structures, Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger inference, LS-means, contrasts, change from baseline, reference-grid estimated marginal means, diagnostics, and worksheet UDFs. Fit a marginal repeated-measures model for continuous longitudinal outcomes and estimate visit-specific means and treatment differences.

Includes: Gaussian linear mixed models, ML / REML, fixed effects with categorical factors, polynomial terms and interactions, random intercepts, random slopes and random-effect interactions, G-side covariance structures (RI, RI+slope, ID, VC/Diag, CS, CSH, AR1, ARH1, TOEP, TOEPH, Unstructured), optional R-side residual covariance structures, Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger inference, fitted values/residuals, BLUPs, covariance/correlation output, diagnostics and trace output. Fit subject- or cluster-level random-effects models for continuous outcomes, including random-intercept, random-slope and richer mixed-model specifications.

Includes: Propensity score estimation by GLM logistic regression or supplied scores; nearest-neighbor, optimal pair, subclassification, weighting, coarsened exact matching, exact matching restrictions, calipers, common support and trimming; ATT / ATC / ATE / ATO estimands; balance diagnostics, Love-plot data, overlap and weight diagnostics, AIPW doubly robust estimates, bootstrap summaries, and Rosenbaum-style matched-pair sensitivity analysis. Estimate treatment effects for observational studies by balancing treated and control groups using propensity-score-based matching, weighting, and diagnostics.
Includes: Paired t-test (matched pairs). Compare two paired measurements on the same subjects by testing the mean of differences.
Includes: Sample size for paired t-test (iterative t critical values). Estimate required number of pairs for a paired t-test given effect size, SD, α and power.

Includes: Paired radius–angle plots, degrees/radians/percentage angles, clockwise or counterclockwise rotation, four zero-angle positions, optional connecting lines, optional text or numeric grouping, automatic radial scaling, configurable radial and angular tick intervals.

Includes: PCA on correlation or covariance matrix, Component extraction: eigenvalue, fixed k, variance threshold, Outputs: scores, loadings, reduced dataset, Plots: scree, score/loading plots, biplots (2D/3D). Reduce dimensionality of multivariate numeric data and visualize dominant patterns.

Includes: Single proportion (estimate + CI), Two independent proportions (Superiority, Noninferiority, Equivalence) (difference + CI, Fisher exact p-values), Two paired proportions (difference + CI, Liddell/McNemar-type test). Work with binomial outcomes: estimate proportions and compare proportions between groups.
Includes: ROC curve points, AUC (Wilcoxon), SE / CI / p-value, Cutoff table. Assess binary classifier performance and explore sensitivity/specificity tradeoffs across thresholds.

Includes: Pearson chi-square test of independence, Nominal association (Cramer's V, Phi, contingency coefficient), Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test (optional), Ordinal association (tau-b/tau-c, gamma, Somers’ D), Cochran–Armitage trend test (when applicable). Analyze general contingency tables and report association measures and exact/trend tests where applicable.

Includes: Sankey Plot. Weighted Sankey/alluvial diagrams, staged row-by-row pathways, Source/Target link tables, optional frequency or continuous positive weights, automatic or explicit stage placement. Visualize how counts, frequencies, or other non-negative quantities flow between categorical states across two or more stages.
Includes: Scatter plot matrix, Optional correlation coefficients, Optional regression lines. Quickly explore pairwise relationships among many variables.

Includes: Sample size planning for a two-group log-rank test. Estimate the required number of events, plus the corresponding numbers of controls, experimental subjects, and total subjects for a study with a time-to-event endpoint.
Includes: Sample size for a single proportion test. Estimate required sample size for testing a single proportion against a null value.
Includes: Skillings–Mack test (handles missing values). Nonparametric test for block designs like Friedman, but robust to missing observations.
Includes: Spearman’s ρ (rank correlation), p-value / CI where applicable. Measure monotonic association between two variables using ranks (robust to non-normality and outliers).
Includes: Miao–Gel–Gastwirth test, Cabilio–Masaro test, Asymmetry plot (optional). Evaluate whether a distribution is symmetric around its center and visualize asymmetry when needed.
Includes: Median slope (Theil–Sen), CI at the selected level (Sen/large-sample approx.), Robust intercept. Use when you want a robust simple linear trend estimate that resists outliers.

Includes: Two-way nested ANOVA, Balanced design check, Satterthwaite approximation. Analyze hierarchical (nested) designs such as subjects nested within centers, with appropriate variance decomposition.
Includes: Grubbs’ test (single outlier), Rosner / generalized ESD (multiple outliers). Identify statistically unusual values in a single variable, with options suited to one or multiple outliers.

Includes: two-sample t-test for superiority, noninferiority, and equivalence (TOST) for two independent means; choice of Welch unequal variances or equal variances (pooled); optional descriptive statistics and box-and-whiskers plot. Compare two independent groups under (or relaxing) the equal-variance assumption.

Includes: Sample size planning for an unpaired two-sample t-test in Superiority, Noninferiority, and Equivalence modes. Estimate required sample sizes per group for a two-sample t-test given effect size, SD, α and power.

Includes: Event-count and subject-count planning for a Cox proportional hazards model with either a binary covariate or a continuous covariate. /nEstimate the required number of events, and when an overall event proportion is supplied, the corresponding number of subjects..

Includes: Sample size planning for a one-sided hypothesis test on an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). /nEstimate the required number of subjects for a study in which each subject is measured repeatedly or rated multiple times.

Includes: Sample size planning for a Bland-Altman agreement study when the goal is to control the confidence-interval half-width around a limit of agreement (LoA). /nEstimate the required number of paired measurements so that the confidence interval around either LoA is sufficiently precise on the original measurement scale.

Includes: Multi-group categorical violin plots, Gaussian kernel-density estimation, Silverman/Scott/manual bandwidths, bandwidth adjustment, configurable density resolution, equal-width/equal-area/sample-size scaling.

Includes: Exact p-values (when available), Normal approximation (ties + continuity correction), Hodges–Lehmann shift estimate, Sign test (optional). Nonparametric paired comparison test for matched samples or before/after measurements.

Includes: 3D scatter plot (X,Y,Z), Optional group coloring, Optional point labels, Rotation/zoom + plane projections (optional). Visualize three-dimensional relationships with interactive rotation controls.

Includes: ZIP model (Poisson count + logistic inflation part), separate authored effects for the Poisson and Logistic components, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, EM-style fitting (with iterations/ε), optional starting values for both parts. Model count data with excess zeros by combining a Poisson model with a separate zero-inflation process.

Includes: Passing–Bablok nonparametric linear regression for method comparison, slope/intercept estimates, confidence intervals, and robust handling of outliers. Use when comparing two measurement methods without assuming normal errors or homoscedasticity.

Includes: Deming (errors-in-variables) regression with configurable error ratio (λ), weighted/generalized variance models, point estimates and confidence intervals. Use when both X and Y have measurement error and you want a symmetric method-comparison regression.

Includes: Simple paired Bland–Altman analysis, repeated-measures Bland–Altman by subject, bias and limits of agreement (LoA), analytical / jackknife / bootstrap confidence intervals, optional proportional-bias check, optional allowable-bias / decision-limit reporting, raw-difference / percentage / log-ratio scales, several x-axis conventions, and Bland–Altman plots with optional subject means.
Includes: Lin CCC, Pearson r, bias-correction factor Cb, analytical or bootstrap confidence intervals, null-concordance test, and identity-line plot.

Includes: Cohen's / weighted kappa for paired categorical ratings, with unweighted, linear, quadratic, Cicchetti–Allison, and Fleiss–Cohen weighting schemes; analytical and bootstrap confidence intervals; confusion-matrix output; and weight-matrix output.
Includes: ICC(1,1), ICC(1,k), ICC(2,1), ICC(2,k), ICC(3,1), ICC(3,k) with confidence intervals. Quantify reliability/agreement of measurements across raters/replicates using standard ICC families.

arm_string_literals: Includes: Pearson chi-square, Fisher’s exact (two-sided, one-sided, mid-p), Odds ratio + CI, Relative risk + CI, McNemar / Liddell test for paired 2×2. Analyze 2×2 contingency tables with exact tests and common effect-size measures.
Includes: Tukey boxplot (median, quartiles, whiskers), Outliers via 1.5×IQR rule. Visualize distribution shape and outliers across one or more groups.
Includes: Bullet Chart. Compare an observed value with a target while simultaneously showing qualitative performance ranges in a compact dashboard-style display.
Includes: Grouped density histograms, stacked density histograms, grouped frequency histograms for unequal sample sizes.
Includes: Cochran’s Q, Percent of 1’s per condition. Test differences in matched binary outcomes across three or more conditions (extension of McNemar).

Includes: Individuals, moving-range, I–MR, X-bar, R, S, X-bar–R, X-bar–S, p, np, c, u, CUSUM, EWMA, and moving-average charts; Phase I and Phase II stages; historical or stage-specific limits; wide and stacked subgroup layouts; exact probability limits for attribute charts; special-cause rule presets and custom rules; explicit exclusions; specification and target lines; detailed chart data, signals, settings, and audit output.
Includes: Convex Hull Plot. Display a point cloud together with the smallest convex boundary containing all observations, either for the complete dataset or separately for each group.
Includes: Correspondence analysis (CA), Row/column contribution plots, Biplot. Explore structure in contingency tables via low-dimensional map representations of rows and columns.

Includes: Cox proportional hazards model, Tie handling: Breslow, Efron, Exact, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, robust variance (optional), residuals + PH score test (optional), baseline + adjusted survival curves. Fit a proportional hazards model to time-to-event data and report hazard ratios with diagnostics.

Includes: Cumulative Distribution Function Plot. Display the cumulative distribution of one or more continuous samples, compare groups across the full distribution, read empirical percentiles, and visually compare observed cumulative behaviour with a fitted theoretical distribution.

Includes: n, mean, median, SD / variance, SEM, CV, skewness / kurtosis, Q1 / Q3, IQR, min / max / range, Shapiro–Wilk (optional). Compute a compact set of summary statistics for one or multiple variables, optionally adding a normality check.

Includes: Linear and quadratic discriminant analysis, group priors, optional preprocessing, posterior probabilities, classification tables, canonical discriminant functions, and leave-one-out / k-fold / holdout validation. Classify observations into known groups and inspect how the groups are separated.

Includes: Dumbbell Plot. Horizontal two-endpoint dumbbell charts, numeric or date/time X axes, optional repeated observations/events. Compare two values for each category while showing both the direction and magnitude of the difference, with optional additional observations displayed along the same horizontal scale.

Includes: Exploratory factor analysis on correlation or covariance matrices; extraction by principal axis, maximum likelihood, generalized least squares, image, alpha, or principal-components style extraction; retention by fixed count / eigenvalue cutoff / cumulative variance; orthogonal or oblique rotation; factor scores; diagnostics; scree and loading plots. Explore latent structure behind correlated numeric variables and inspect communalities, loadings, scores, and residual matrices.

Includes: Friedman test, Post-hoc multiple comparisons (MCP), Descriptive stats (optional), Box plot (optional). Nonparametric repeated-measures alternative to one-way RM ANOVA for ranked data across conditions.

Includes: Families: Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Negative Binomial, Gamma, Covariance structures: Independence, Exchangeable, Autoregressive, Toeplitz, Unstructured, SE types: Robust, Naive, Bias-reduced, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values. Includes: RM ANOVA, Sphericity: Mauchly test (optional), Corrections: Greenhouse–Geisser, Huynh–Feldt (optional), Post-hoc: Tukey (optional), Descriptive stats / box plot (optional). Compare means across repeated conditions for the same subjects, with optional sphericity diagnostics and corrections.

Includes: Ordinal logistic regression, Reference category selection (first/last), categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, optional offset/weights, covariance matrix, residuals. Model ordered categorical outcomes using an ordinal logistic framework.

Includes: Gaussian MMRM, ML / REML, subject-level residual covariance structures, Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger inference, LS-means, contrasts, change from baseline, reference-grid estimated marginal means, diagnostics, and worksheet UDFs. Fit a marginal repeated-measures model for continuous longitudinal outcomes and estimate visit-specific means and treatment differences.

Includes: Gaussian linear mixed models, ML / REML, fixed effects with categorical factors, polynomial terms and interactions, random intercepts, random slopes and random-effect interactions, G-side covariance structures (RI, RI+slope, ID, VC/Diag, CS, CSH, AR1, ARH1, TOEP, TOEPH, Unstructured), optional R-side residual covariance structures, Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger inference, fitted values/residuals, BLUPs, covariance/correlation output, diagnostics and trace output. Fit subject- or cluster-level random-effects models for continuous outcomes, including random-intercept, random-slope and richer mixed-model specifications.

Includes: Propensity score estimation by GLM logistic regression or supplied scores; nearest-neighbor, optimal pair, subclassification, weighting, coarsened exact matching, exact matching restrictions, calipers, common support and trimming; ATT / ATC / ATE / ATO estimands; balance diagnostics, Love-plot data, overlap and weight diagnostics, AIPW doubly robust estimates, bootstrap summaries, and Rosenbaum-style matched-pair sensitivity analysis. Estimate treatment effects for observational studies by balancing treated and control groups using propensity-score-based matching, weighting, and diagnostics.
Includes: Paired t-test (matched pairs). Compare two paired measurements on the same subjects by testing the mean of differences.
Includes: Sample size for paired t-test (iterative t critical values). Estimate required number of pairs for a paired t-test given effect size, SD, α and power.

Includes: Paired radius–angle plots, degrees/radians/percentage angles, clockwise or counterclockwise rotation, four zero-angle positions, optional connecting lines, optional text or numeric grouping, automatic radial scaling, configurable radial and angular tick intervals.

Includes: PCA on correlation or covariance matrix, Component extraction: eigenvalue, fixed k, variance threshold, Outputs: scores, loadings, reduced dataset, Plots: scree, score/loading plots, biplots (2D/3D). Reduce dimensionality of multivariate numeric data and visualize dominant patterns.

Includes: Single proportion (estimate + CI), Two independent proportions (Superiority, Noninferiority, Equivalence) (difference + CI, Fisher exact p-values), Two paired proportions (difference + CI, Liddell/McNemar-type test). Work with binomial outcomes: estimate proportions and compare proportions between groups.
Includes: ROC curve points, AUC (Wilcoxon), SE / CI / p-value, Cutoff table. Assess binary classifier performance and explore sensitivity/specificity tradeoffs across thresholds.

Includes: Pearson chi-square test of independence, Nominal association (Cramer's V, Phi, contingency coefficient), Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test (optional), Ordinal association (tau-b/tau-c, gamma, Somers’ D), Cochran–Armitage trend test (when applicable). Analyze general contingency tables and report association measures and exact/trend tests where applicable.

Includes: Sankey Plot. Weighted Sankey/alluvial diagrams, staged row-by-row pathways, Source/Target link tables, optional frequency or continuous positive weights, automatic or explicit stage placement. Visualize how counts, frequencies, or other non-negative quantities flow between categorical states across two or more stages.
Includes: Scatter plot matrix, Optional correlation coefficients, Optional regression lines. Quickly explore pairwise relationships among many variables.

Includes: Sample size planning for a two-group log-rank test. Estimate the required number of events, plus the corresponding numbers of controls, experimental subjects, and total subjects for a study with a time-to-event endpoint.
Includes: Sample size for a single proportion test. Estimate required sample size for testing a single proportion against a null value.
Includes: Skillings–Mack test (handles missing values). Nonparametric test for block designs like Friedman, but robust to missing observations.
Includes: Spearman’s ρ (rank correlation), p-value / CI where applicable. Measure monotonic association between two variables using ranks (robust to non-normality and outliers).
Includes: Miao–Gel–Gastwirth test, Cabilio–Masaro test, Asymmetry plot (optional). Evaluate whether a distribution is symmetric around its center and visualize asymmetry when needed.
Includes: Median slope (Theil–Sen), CI at the selected level (Sen/large-sample approx.), Robust intercept. Use when you want a robust simple linear trend estimate that resists outliers.

Includes: Two-way nested ANOVA, Balanced design check, Satterthwaite approximation. Analyze hierarchical (nested) designs such as subjects nested within centers, with appropriate variance decomposition.
Includes: Grubbs’ test (single outlier), Rosner / generalized ESD (multiple outliers). Identify statistically unusual values in a single variable, with options suited to one or multiple outliers.

Includes: two-sample t-test for superiority, noninferiority, and equivalence (TOST) for two independent means; choice of Welch unequal variances or equal variances (pooled); optional descriptive statistics and box-and-whiskers plot. Compare two independent groups under (or relaxing) the equal-variance assumption.

Includes: Sample size planning for an unpaired two-sample t-test in Superiority, Noninferiority, and Equivalence modes. Estimate required sample sizes per group for a two-sample t-test given effect size, SD, α and power.

Includes: Event-count and subject-count planning for a Cox proportional hazards model with either a binary covariate or a continuous covariate. /nEstimate the required number of events, and when an overall event proportion is supplied, the corresponding number of subjects..

Includes: Sample size planning for a one-sided hypothesis test on an intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). /nEstimate the required number of subjects for a study in which each subject is measured repeatedly or rated multiple times.

Includes: Sample size planning for a Bland-Altman agreement study when the goal is to control the confidence-interval half-width around a limit of agreement (LoA). /nEstimate the required number of paired measurements so that the confidence interval around either LoA is sufficiently precise on the original measurement scale.

Includes: Multi-group categorical violin plots, Gaussian kernel-density estimation, Silverman/Scott/manual bandwidths, bandwidth adjustment, configurable density resolution, equal-width/equal-area/sample-size scaling.

Includes: Exact p-values (when available), Normal approximation (ties + continuity correction), Hodges–Lehmann shift estimate, Sign test (optional). Nonparametric paired comparison test for matched samples or before/after measurements.

Includes: 3D scatter plot (X,Y,Z), Optional group coloring, Optional point labels, Rotation/zoom + plane projections (optional). Visualize three-dimensional relationships with interactive rotation controls.

Includes: ZIP model (Poisson count + logistic inflation part), separate authored effects for the Poisson and Logistic components, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, EM-style fitting (with iterations/ε), optional starting values for both parts. Model count data with excess zeros by combining a Poisson model with a separate zero-inflation process.

Includes: Passing–Bablok nonparametric linear regression for method comparison, slope/intercept estimates, confidence intervals, and robust handling of outliers. Use when comparing two measurement methods without assuming normal errors or homoscedasticity.

Includes: Deming (errors-in-variables) regression with configurable error ratio (λ), weighted/generalized variance models, point estimates and confidence intervals. Use when both X and Y have measurement error and you want a symmetric method-comparison regression.

Includes: Simple paired Bland–Altman analysis, repeated-measures Bland–Altman by subject, bias and limits of agreement (LoA), analytical / jackknife / bootstrap confidence intervals, optional proportional-bias check, optional allowable-bias / decision-limit reporting, raw-difference / percentage / log-ratio scales, several x-axis conventions, and Bland–Altman plots with optional subject means.
Includes: Lin CCC, Pearson r, bias-correction factor Cb, analytical or bootstrap confidence intervals, null-concordance test, and identity-line plot.

Includes: Cohen's / weighted kappa for paired categorical ratings, with unweighted, linear, quadratic, Cicchetti–Allison, and Fleiss–Cohen weighting schemes; analytical and bootstrap confidence intervals; confusion-matrix output; and weight-matrix output.
Includes: ICC(1,1), ICC(1,k), ICC(2,1), ICC(2,k), ICC(3,1), ICC(3,k) with confidence intervals. Quantify reliability/agreement of measurements across raters/replicates using standard ICC families.

arm_string_literals: Includes: Pearson chi-square, Fisher’s exact (two-sided, one-sided, mid-p), Odds ratio + CI, Relative risk + CI, McNemar / Liddell test for paired 2×2. Analyze 2×2 contingency tables with exact tests and common effect-size measures.
Includes: Tukey boxplot (median, quartiles, whiskers), Outliers via 1.5×IQR rule. Visualize distribution shape and outliers across one or more groups.
Includes: Bullet Chart. Compare an observed value with a target while simultaneously showing qualitative performance ranges in a compact dashboard-style display.
Includes: Grouped density histograms, stacked density histograms, grouped frequency histograms for unequal sample sizes.
Includes: Cochran’s Q, Percent of 1’s per condition. Test differences in matched binary outcomes across three or more conditions (extension of McNemar).

Includes: Individuals, moving-range, I–MR, X-bar, R, S, X-bar–R, X-bar–S, p, np, c, u, CUSUM, EWMA, and moving-average charts; Phase I and Phase II stages; historical or stage-specific limits; wide and stacked subgroup layouts; exact probability limits for attribute charts; special-cause rule presets and custom rules; explicit exclusions; specification and target lines; detailed chart data, signals, settings, and audit output.
Includes: Convex Hull Plot. Display a point cloud together with the smallest convex boundary containing all observations, either for the complete dataset or separately for each group.
Includes: Correspondence analysis (CA), Row/column contribution plots, Biplot. Explore structure in contingency tables via low-dimensional map representations of rows and columns.

Includes: Cox proportional hazards model, Tie handling: Breslow, Efron, Exact, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values, robust variance (optional), residuals + PH score test (optional), baseline + adjusted survival curves. Fit a proportional hazards model to time-to-event data and report hazard ratios with diagnostics.

Includes: Cumulative Distribution Function Plot. Display the cumulative distribution of one or more continuous samples, compare groups across the full distribution, read empirical percentiles, and visually compare observed cumulative behaviour with a fitted theoretical distribution.

Includes: n, mean, median, SD / variance, SEM, CV, skewness / kurtosis, Q1 / Q3, IQR, min / max / range, Shapiro–Wilk (optional). Compute a compact set of summary statistics for one or multiple variables, optionally adding a normality check.

Includes: Linear and quadratic discriminant analysis, group priors, optional preprocessing, posterior probabilities, classification tables, canonical discriminant functions, and leave-one-out / k-fold / holdout validation. Classify observations into known groups and inspect how the groups are separated.

Includes: Dumbbell Plot. Horizontal two-endpoint dumbbell charts, numeric or date/time X axes, optional repeated observations/events. Compare two values for each category while showing both the direction and magnitude of the difference, with optional additional observations displayed along the same horizontal scale.

Includes: Exploratory factor analysis on correlation or covariance matrices; extraction by principal axis, maximum likelihood, generalized least squares, image, alpha, or principal-components style extraction; retention by fixed count / eigenvalue cutoff / cumulative variance; orthogonal or oblique rotation; factor scores; diagnostics; scree and loading plots. Explore latent structure behind correlated numeric variables and inspect communalities, loadings, scores, and residual matrices.

Includes: Friedman test, Post-hoc multiple comparisons (MCP), Descriptive stats (optional), Box plot (optional). Nonparametric repeated-measures alternative to one-way RM ANOVA for ranked data across conditions.

Includes: Families: Gaussian, Binomial, Poisson, Negative Binomial, Gamma, Covariance structures: Independence, Exchangeable, Autoregressive, Toeplitz, Unstructured, SE types: Robust, Naive, Bias-reduced, categorical factors, polynomial terms, continuous and categorical-factor interactions, optional starting values. Fit marginal models for correlated/clustered data using GEE with selectable working correlation.

Fit generalized linear models to a wide range of outcome types with configurable link functions.

Includes: Agglomerative hierarchical clustering, linkage methods (Ward, complete, average, weighted average, single, centroid, median), distance metrics (squared Euclidean, Euclidean, Manhattan, Chebyshev, Minkowski, cosine, correlation), optional preprocessing, cluster membership by cluster count or cut height, and dendrogram plotting. Namespace ExcelCommon.Chart34
Public NotInheritable Class HullChartSettings34
Public ReadOnly Property SeriesName As String
Public Sub New(Optional inputSeriesName As String = "Data")
Me.SeriesName = inputSeriesName
End Sub
End Class
Public Module HullChartPreparation34


    Public Function ResolveSeriesName(group As ConvexHullPlotGroup,
                                              groupIndex As Integer,
                                              hasGrouping As Boolean,
                                              appearance As HullChartSettings34) As String
        If hasGrouping Then
            If Not String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(group.Name) Then Return group.Name
            Return "Group " & (groupIndex + 1).ToString(CultureInfo.CurrentCulture)
        End If
        Return If(String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(appearance.SeriesName), "Data", appearance.SeriesName.Trim())
    End Function

    ''' <summary>
    ''' Shared Kruskal-Wallis application service. It owns the host-neutral test and optional
    ''' Dunn/Bonferroni post-hoc orchestration so Excel-DNA and Office.js hosts submit the same
    ''' grouped-data contract and receive the same ResultTable output.
    ''' </summary>
    Public NotInheritable Class KruskalWallisApplicationService

        Private Sub New()
        End Sub

        Public Shared Function Run(input As SpreadsheetRangeData) As KruskalWallisApplicationResult
            Return Run(GroupedNumericRangeParser.Parse(input), Nothing)
        End Function

        Public Shared Function Run(input As SpreadsheetRangeData,
                                   options As KruskalWallisAnalysisOptions) As KruskalWallisApplicationResult
            Return Run(GroupedNumericRangeParser.Parse(input), options)
        End Function

        Public Shared Function Run(grouped As GroupedNumericData) As KruskalWallisApplicationResult
            Return Run(grouped, Nothing)
        End Function

        Public Shared Function Run(grouped As GroupedNumericData,
                                   options As KruskalWallisAnalysisOptions) As KruskalWallisApplicationResult
            If grouped Is Nothing Then Throw New ArgumentNullException(NameOf(grouped))

            Dim safeOptions As KruskalWallisAnalysisOptions = NormalizeOptions(options)
            Dim model As New Global.BESHStatNG.nonparametric.KruskallWalis(grouped.Groups, grouped.GroupNames)
            Dim testResult As Global.BESHStatNG.TestResult = model.compute()

            If safeOptions.IncludeDunnComparisons Then
                model.MCP(safeOptions.Alpha)
            End If

            Dim resultTables As List(Of Global.BESHStatNG.ResultTable) = model.wrapResults()
            If resultTables Is Nothing OrElse resultTables.Count = 0 Then
                Throw New InvalidOperationException("Kruskal-Wallis did not produce a ResultTable.")
            End If

            Dim outputTables As New List(Of Global.BESHStatNG.ResultTableOutputModel)(resultTables.Count)
            For Each table As Global.BESHStatNG.ResultTable In resultTables
                outputTables.Add(table.ToOutputModel())
            Next

            Return New KruskalWallisApplicationResult(
                outputTables,
                testResult.TestStatistics1,
                testResult.TestStatistics2,
                testResult.Pvalue,
                testResult.Pvalue2,
                DirectCast(grouped.GroupNames.Clone(), String()),
                grouped.GroupCounts)
        End Function

        Private Shared Function NormalizeOptions(options As KruskalWallisAnalysisOptions) As KruskalWallisAnalysisOptions
            Dim source As KruskalWallisAnalysisOptions = If(options, New KruskalWallisAnalysisOptions())
            Dim safeAlpha As Double = source.Alpha

            If Double.IsNaN(safeAlpha) OrElse Double.IsInfinity(safeAlpha) OrElse
               safeAlpha <= 0.0 OrElse safeAlpha >= 1.0 Then
                safeAlpha = 0.05
            End If

            Return New KruskalWallisAnalysisOptions With {
                .IncludeDunnComparisons = source.IncludeDunnComparisons,
                .Alpha = safeAlpha
            }
        End Function
    End Class

    Public Function ResolveAxisContext(result As LadderPlotResult,
                                               appearance As LadderChartSettings34) As AxisContext
        Dim dataMinimum As Double = result.MinimumValue
        Dim dataMaximum As Double = result.MaximumValue
        If Not IsFinite(dataMinimum) OrElse Not IsFinite(dataMaximum) Then
            Throw New ArgumentException("The ladder result does not contain a finite Y range.", NameOf(result))
        End If

        Dim span As Double = dataMaximum - dataMinimum
        Dim fallbackSpan As Double = If(span > 0.0R,
                                        span,
                                        Math.Max(1.0R, Math.Abs(dataMinimum) * 0.1R))
        If Not IsFinitePositive(fallbackSpan) Then fallbackSpan = 1.0R

        Dim padding As Double = fallbackSpan * appearance.YAxisPaddingFraction
        Dim paddedMinimum As Double = dataMinimum - padding
        Dim paddedMaximum As Double = dataMaximum + padding
        If paddedMinimum >= paddedMaximum Then
            paddedMinimum = dataMinimum - 0.5R * fallbackSpan
            paddedMaximum = dataMaximum + 0.5R * fallbackSpan
        End If

        Dim majorUnit As Double
        If appearance.YAxisMajorUnit.HasValue Then
            majorUnit = appearance.YAxisMajorUnit.Value
        Else
            majorUnit = NiceStep125((paddedMaximum - paddedMinimum) / 5.0R)
        End If
        If Not IsFinitePositive(majorUnit) Then majorUnit = 1.0R

        Dim yMinimum As Double
        If appearance.YAxisMinimum.HasValue Then
            yMinimum = appearance.YAxisMinimum.Value
        Else
            yMinimum = FloorToStep(paddedMinimum, majorUnit)
            If appearance.YAxisIncludeZero AndAlso dataMinimum >= 0.0R Then yMinimum = Math.Min(0.0R, yMinimum)
        End If

        Dim yMaximum As Double
        If appearance.YAxisMaximum.HasValue Then
            yMaximum = appearance.YAxisMaximum.Value
        Else
            yMaximum = CeilingToStep(paddedMaximum, majorUnit)
            If appearance.YAxisIncludeZero AndAlso dataMaximum <= 0.0R Then yMaximum = Math.Max(0.0R, yMaximum)
        End If

        If yMinimum >= yMaximum Then
            If Not appearance.YAxisMinimum.HasValue AndAlso Not appearance.YAxisMaximum.HasValue Then
                yMinimum = FloorToStep(dataMinimum - 0.5R * fallbackSpan, majorUnit)
                yMaximum = CeilingToStep(dataMaximum + 0.5R * fallbackSpan, majorUnit)
                If yMinimum >= yMaximum Then yMaximum = yMinimum + majorUnit
            Else
                Throw New ArgumentException("The resolved Y-axis minimum must be smaller than the Y-axis maximum.", NameOf(appearance))
            End If
        End If

        Return New AxisContext With {
            .XMinimum = PlotXMinimum,
            .XMaximum = PlotXMaximum,
            .YMinimum = yMinimum,
            .YMaximum = yMaximum,
            .YMajorUnit = majorUnit,
            .YNumberFormat = ResolveYAxisNumberFormat(appearance.YAxisNumberFormat)
        }
    End Function
    Public Function ResolveYAxisNumberFormat(requestedFormat As String) As String
        If String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(requestedFormat) Then Return "0.###"
        Return requestedFormat.Trim()
    End Function
    Public Function NiceStep125(rawStep As Double) As Double
        If Not IsFinitePositive(rawStep) Then Return 1.0R

        Dim exponent As Double = Math.Floor(Math.Log10(rawStep))
        Dim scale As Double = Math.Pow(10.0R, exponent)
        Dim fraction As Double = rawStep / scale
        Dim niceFraction As Double

        If fraction <= 1.0R Then
            niceFraction = 1.0R
        ElseIf fraction <= 2.0R Then
            niceFraction = 2.0R
        ElseIf fraction <= 5.0R Then
            niceFraction = 5.0R
        Else
            niceFraction = 10.0R
        End If

        Return niceFraction * scale
    End Function
    Public Function FloorToStep(value As Double, stepSize As Double) As Double
        Return Math.Floor(value / stepSize) * stepSize
    End Function
    Public Function CeilingToStep(value As Double, stepSize As Double) As Double
        Return Math.Ceiling(value / stepSize) * stepSize
    End Function
    Public Function BuildEndpointLabel(observation As LadderPlotObservation,
                                               useFirstSide As Boolean,
                                               appearance As LadderChartSettings34) As String
        Dim value As Double = If(useFirstSide, observation.FirstValue, observation.SecondValue)
        Dim valueText As String = FormatEndpointValue(value, appearance.EndpointValueDisplayFormat)

        Select Case appearance.EndpointLabelContent
            Case LadderEndpointLabelContent.Value
                Return valueText
            Case LadderEndpointLabelContent.RecordLabel
                Return observation.RecordLabel
            Case LadderEndpointLabelContent.RecordLabelAndValue
                Dim separator As String = If(appearance.EndpointLabelSeparator, String.Empty)
                Return observation.RecordLabel & separator & valueText
            Case Else
                Return observation.RecordLabel & ", " & valueText
        End Select
    End Function
    Public Function FormatEndpointValue(value As Double, requestedFormat As String) As String
        If Not String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(requestedFormat) Then
            Try
                Return value.ToString(requestedFormat.Trim(), CultureInfo.CurrentCulture)
            Catch ex As FormatException
                'Fall through to a compact default rather than failing chart creation for
                'an invalid cosmetic display format.
            End Try
        End If
        Return value.ToString("0.###", CultureInfo.CurrentCulture)
    End Function
    Public Function ResolveObservationSeriesName(observation As LadderPlotObservation,
                                                         appearance As LadderChartSettings34) As String
        Select Case appearance.ColorMode
            Case LadderColorMode.ByObservation
                If Not String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(observation.RecordLabel) Then Return observation.RecordLabel
                Return "Observation " & (observation.DisplayIndex + 1).ToString(CultureInfo.CurrentCulture)
            Case LadderColorMode.ByGroup
                If Not String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(observation.GroupLabel) Then Return observation.GroupLabel
                Return "Group " & (observation.GroupLevelIndex + 1).ToString(CultureInfo.CurrentCulture)
            Case Else
                If String.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(appearance.SeriesName) Then Return "Data"
                Return appearance.SeriesName.Trim()
        End Select
    End Function
    Public Function SuggestedWidth(result As LadderPlotResult,
                                          Optional appearance As LadderChartSettings34 = Nothing) As Double
        Dim resolved As LadderChartSettings34 = If(appearance, New LadderChartSettings34())
        If resolved.ShowFirstEndpointLabels OrElse resolved.ShowSecondEndpointLabels Then Return 820.0R
        Return 620.0R
    End Function
    Public Function SuggestedHeight(result As LadderPlotResult,
                                           Optional appearance As LadderChartSettings34 = Nothing) As Double
        If result Is Nothing OrElse result.ObservationCount < 1 Then Return 420.0R
        Dim resolved As LadderChartSettings34 = If(appearance, New LadderChartSettings34())
        If resolved.ShowFirstEndpointLabels OrElse resolved.ShowSecondEndpointLabels Then
            Return Math.Max(420.0R, Math.Min(1200.0R, 210.0R + 17.0R * result.ObservationCount))
        End If
        Return 440.0R
    End Function
    Private Function IsFinite(value As Double) As Boolean
        Return Not Double.IsNaN(value) AndAlso Not Double.IsInfinity(value)
    End Function
    Private Function IsFinitePositive(value As Double) As Boolean
        Return IsFinite(value) AndAlso value > 0.0R
    End Function

Public Function ResolveAxisContext(result As LadderPlotResult,
                                               appearance As LadderChartSettings34) As AxisContext
        Dim dataMinimum As Double = result.MinimumValue
        Dim dataMaximum As Double = result.MaximumValue
        If Not IsFinite(dataMinimum) OrElse Not IsFinite(dataMaximum) Then
            Throw New ArgumentException("The ladder result does not contain a finite Y range.", NameOf(result))
        End If

        Dim span As Double = dataMaximum - dataMinimum
        Dim fallbackSpan As Double = If(span > 0.0R,
                                        span,
                                        Math.Max(1.0R, Math.Abs(dataMinimum) * 0.1R))
        If Not IsFinitePositive(fallbackSpan) Then fallbackSpan = 1.0R

        Dim padding As Double = fallbackSpan * appearance.YAxisPaddingFraction
        Dim paddedMinimum As Double = dataMinimum - padding
        Dim paddedMaximum As Double = dataMaximum + padding
        If paddedMinimum >= paddedMaximum Then
            paddedMinimum = dataMinimum - 0.5R * fallbackSpan
            paddedMaximum = dataMaximum + 0.5R * fallbackSpan
        End If

        Dim majorUnit As Double
        If appearance.YAxisMajorUnit.HasValue Then
            majorUnit = appearance.YAxisMajorUnit.Value
        Else
            majorUnit = NiceStep125((paddedMaximum - paddedMinimum) / 5.0R)
        End If
        If Not IsFinitePositive(majorUnit) Then majorUnit = 1.0R

        Dim yMinimum As Double
        If appearance.YAxisMinimum.HasValue Then
            yMinimum = appearance.YAxisMinimum.Value
        Else
            yMinimum = FloorToStep(paddedMinimum, majorUnit)
            If appearance.YAxisIncludeZero AndAlso dataMinimum >= 0.0R Then yMinimum = Math.Min(0.0R, yMinimum)
        End If

        Dim yMaximum As Double
        If appearance.YAxisMaximum.HasValue Then
            yMaximum = appearance.YAxisMaximum.Value
        Else
            yMaximum = CeilingToStep(paddedMaximum, majorUnit)
            If appearance.YAxisIncludeZero AndAlso dataMaximum <= 0.0R Then yMaximum = Math.Max(0.0R, yMaximum)
        End If

        If yMinimum >= yMaximum Then
            If Not appearance.YAxisMinimum.HasValue AndAlso Not appearance.YAxisMaximum.HasValue Then
                yMinimum = FloorToStep(dataMinimum - 0.5R * fallbackSpan, majorUnit)
                yMaximum = CeilingToStep(dataMaximum + 0.5R * fallbackSpan, majorUnit)
                If yMinimum >= yMaximum Then yMaximum = yMinimum + majorUnit
            Else
                Throw New ArgumentException("The resolved Y-axis minimum must be smaller than the Y-axis maximum.", NameOf(appearance))
            End If
        End If

        Return New AxisContext With {
            .XMinimum = PlotXMinimum,
            .XMaximum = PlotXMaximum,
            .YMinimum = yMinimum,
            .YMaximum = yMaximum,
            .YMajorUnit = majorUnit,
            .YNumberFormat = ResolveYAxisNumberFormat(appearance.YAxisNumberFormat)
        }
    End Function

Public Function NiceStep125(rawStep As Double) As Double
        If Not IsFinitePositive(rawStep) Then Return 1.0R

        Dim exponent As Double = Math.Floor(Math.Log10(rawStep))
        Dim scale As Double = Math.Pow(10.0R, exponent)
        Dim fraction As Double = rawStep / scale
        Dim niceFraction As Double

        If fraction <= 1.0R Then
            niceFraction = 1.0R
        ElseIf fraction <= 2.0R Then
            niceFraction = 2.0R
        ElseIf fraction <= 5.0R Then
            niceFraction = 5.0R
        Else
            niceFraction = 10.0R
        End If

        Return niceFraction * scale
    End Function

Public Function EndpointAnchors(observations As LadderPlotObservation(), useFirstSide As Boolean, minimum As Double, maximum As Double, gap As Double) As SeriesPayload34
        Dim maximumObservedJitter As Double = 0.0R
        For i As Integer = 0 To observations.Length - 1
            Dim offset As Double = If(useFirstSide,
                                      Math.Abs(observations(i).FirstJitterOffset),
                                      Math.Abs(observations(i).SecondJitterOffset))
            maximumObservedJitter = Math.Max(maximumObservedJitter, offset)
        Next

        Dim anchorX As Double
        If useFirstSide Then
            anchorX = LadderPlotCore.FirstBaseXPosition - maximumObservedJitter - gap
            anchorX = Math.Max(minimum + 0.02R, anchorX)
        Else
            anchorX = LadderPlotCore.SecondBaseXPosition + maximumObservedJitter + gap
            anchorX = Math.Min(maximum - 0.02R, anchorX)
        End If

        Dim xValues(observations.Length - 1) As Double
        For i As Integer = 0 To xValues.Length - 1
            xValues(i) = anchorX
        Next

Return New SeriesPayload34(xValues, New Double(){}, source:=observations.Select(Function(c) c.SourceIndex).ToArray())
End Function

Public Function MinimumSeparation(plotHeight As Double, requestedChartHeight As Double, minimum As Double, maximum As Double, minimumPoints As Double, fontSize As Double) As Double
        If Not IsFinitePositive(plotHeight) Then
            plotHeight = Math.Max(120.0R, requestedChartHeight * 0.7R)
        End If

        Dim desiredPoints As Double = Math.Max(minimumPoints,
                                               fontSize * 1.25R)
        Dim axisSpan As Double = maximum - minimum
        If Not IsFinitePositive(axisSpan) Then Return 0.0R

        Return axisSpan * desiredPoints / plotHeight

        Dim maximumObservedJitter As Double = 0.0R
        For i As Integer = 0 To observations.Length - 1

        Next

        Private Sub New()
        End Sub
        Public Shared Function Supports(request As RegressionRequest) As Boolean
            Return request IsNot Nothing AndAlso (request.Kind = RegressionAnalysisKind.LinearModel OrElse
                (request.Kind = RegressionAnalysisKind.GeneralizedLinearModel AndAlso
                 request.Options.Family.HasValue AndAlso
                 (request.Options.Family.Value = RegressionFamily.Gaussian OrElse request.Options.Family.Value = RegressionFamily.Binomial)))
        End Function
        ''' <summary>Retain the accepted four-argument CLR entry point for already compiled
        ''' consumers. Source callers can also use the additive optional alpha-mode overload.</summary>
        Public Shared Overloads Function Project(request As RegressionRequest, sums As TermSumOfSquaresType,
